### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/system/demo-staff.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/system/demo-staff.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45de8c6cbac1318e9aa2b1bc25013aa908d2d0c8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ce105fd04bf3e5bcf24d4c05d558d0633c4e7aef` — the merge of head `4b28e26533f934179cc4e09dffb256b680ec6aa6` into base `45de8c6cbac1318e9aa2b1bc25013aa908d2d0c8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ce105fd04bf3e5bcf24d4c05d558d0633c4e7aef && git checkout ce105fd04bf3e5bcf24d4c05d558d0633c4e7aef
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45de8c6cbac1318e9aa2b1bc25013aa908d2d0c8 4b28e26533f934179cc4e09dffb256b680ec6aa6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45de8c6cbac1318e9aa2b1bc25013aa908d2d0c8 && git merge --no-ff 4b28e26533f934179cc4e09dffb256b680ec6aa6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45de8c6cbac1318e9aa2b1bc25013aa908d2d0c8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4b28e26533f934179cc4e09dffb256b680ec6aa6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/demo-staff.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/dev-login.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts (`SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT`), packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts (`SEED_WRITE_OPTIONS`, the two basic-insert fallbacks, `demoStaffingArmed`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts (`SeedLoaderService.SEED_OPTIONS`; `packages/runtime/src/seed-loader.ts` is its re-export shim), packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts (`buildSession`), packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.seed.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-write-guard.ts and its test, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/dev-admin-seed-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/demo-staff.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts (`maybeProvisionDemoStaff`), packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts (the `demoStaff` hand-over), packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts (`os dev` spawns `serve --dev`), docs/adr/0092-sys-user-profile-field-delegation.md (D2), content/docs/references/system/dev-login.mdx, .changeset/26424-demo-staff-dev-login-seed-prose.md, skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:446 (read for ③ only)

### ① Derived judgments

Every hunk in the two `hits` paths sits inside a block comment, a `guidance` string value of the `strictObject` options, or the string argument of one `.describe()`. No key, validator, alias, default, export or type moved; `email` stays `z.string().email()`; the `aliases` and `history` maps are byte-identical. Derived accept-set and public-surface changes: **none, prose only** — right. `check:authorable-surface` and `check:api-surface` have nothing to move; `check:docs` is the one artifact gate the diff reaches, and the regenerated `dev-login.mdx` `email` row is byte-equal to the new `.describe()` string, so the mdx matches the describes. `demo-staff.mdx` renders only field describes, none of which changed, so it is correctly untouched.

Each new sentence judged against the cited code:

- "every seed write runs under the system execution context" — **true.** `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT` is `{ isSystem: true, skipTriggers: true, seedReplay: true }` (execution-context.zod.ts L630). `app-plugin.ts` L56 wraps it as `SEED_WRITE_OPTIONS` and both basic-insert fallbacks (L2052, L2072) pass it; the main path is `SeedLoaderService`, whose `SEED_OPTIONS` (metadata-protocol seed-loader.ts L2771) wraps the same export, and its few inline contexts (L2214, L2396, L3559, L3592) are `isSystem: true` too.
- "which ADR-0092's identity-write guard stands aside for" / "is not refused" — **true.** `isUserContextWrite(session)` is `Boolean(session?.userId) && session?.isSystem !== true` (identity-write-guard.ts); `buildSession` carries `isSystem` through (engine-execution-plumbing.ts L56) and a seed context carries no `userId`, so the guard returns before throwing on both grounds. ADR-0092 D2 says the same ("Internal writes ... `isSystem` plugin/system contexts bypass untouched"); pinned at identity-write-guard.test.ts L84 and L378. No other guard refuses it: plugin-security's ADR-0103 `system-write-guard` covers only the `engine-owned`/`append-only` buckets, and `sys_user` is `managedBy: 'better-auth'`.
- "lands as a directory row with no account, and it cannot sign in" — **true.** `app-plugin.seed.test.ts` L79/L113 pin the `sys_user` insert being issued with the seed options; `dev-admin-seed-gate.ts` header records the end-to-end measurement the sentence restates (13 `sys_user` rows, zero `sys_account` rows, `POST /auth/sign-in/email` → 401) and is the module that was written to close exactly that consequence.
- "declare the person in `demoStaff` so `os dev` creates the account" / "through the auth door, so it can sign in" — **true.** `os dev` spawns `serve --dev` (dev.ts L215); serve.ts L4366 hands the authored `demoStaff` to `AuthPlugin`; `maybeProvisionDemoStaff` (auth-plugin.ts L2455–2535) runs at `kernel:ready` after the dev admin and creates each entry with `api.signUpEmail` under an operator-provisioning ticket, so the account carries a credential. Conditional on the three gates in demo-staff.ts (development boot, loopback base URL, `single` posture, a prior login); the `devLogins` text states the result unconditionally, but the gates are documented in the `demoStaff` TSDoc it points at, so the pointer is accurate enough for its purpose. Observation, not a finding.
- "`os dev` creates the account" wording in the `seed` prescription replaces "or in `onEnable`" — right: `onEnable` is not a kernel hook here (AGENTS.md → Patterns), so the old prescription named a door that does not exist.

Card acceptance, read on the head tree: `refused (ADR-0092)` in demo-staff.zod.ts → 0; `in \`data\`` in dev-login.zod.ts → 0 (control `through \`data\`` → 2, so the grep reads the file); `demoStaff` in dev-login.zod.ts → 5; `dev-login.mdx` regenerated in the same PR. All met.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/26424-demo-staff-dev-login-seed-prose.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines. The diff publishes prose and one refusal prescription's wording from a released package and no protocol change, so `none` takes `patch` and the `Clause-②: no` line matches a diff that neither widens nor narrows what an author can write — **right.** No `skip-changeset`, no BREAKING banner owed, no ADR-0087 disposition owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- os-dev report (comment 6434751423): `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings` 1: `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:446` still reads "a `sys_user` row in `data` is refused (ADR-0092)" at this head (read, confirmed). The card's acceptance clause "the objectstack-platform skill's sentence (PR #26420's patch round) agrees with the new TSDoc" is a cross-PR condition the card itself assigns to #26420's patch round; this PR cannot meet it and is not asked to. **Escalated** to the `domain:skills` seat that owns #26420: that round must land the agreeing sentence, and until it does the skill and the spec disagree. Not a FAIL of this head.
- PR body "Surface additions, accepted by seat 1 at claim time" (the dev-login header TSDoc and the `email` describe): the Claim (comment 6434400794) lists the dev-login surface as "the guidance strings at L64-74 only" and records no such acceptance; no later card comment does either. Judged on the card's own text instead: Wanted (2) asks that the describe text "stop prescribing a `data` seed" and name `demoStaff` "so the regenerated `dev-login.mdx` follows", and the acceptance clause requires `demoStaff` "named in its describe text" and the mdx regenerated. Only the `email` `.describe()` reaches the generated reference, so the card cannot be met without it, and the header TSDoc is the same false sentence family ("`data` fixtures" as the way to have the account) the card's title names. **Answered: the widening is the card's, and the claim's L64-74 restriction was narrower than the card.** The dev's report explains it, as the claim's "stop on a breach and explain it" asks.
- Premise correction in the report (L67/L71/L73 are `strictObject` `guidance` entries, not `.describe()` text): verified on the head tree — they are values of the `guidance` map and surface only in an unknown-key refusal. **Answered**, and it is why the `email` describe had to join the surface.
- Cosmetic, no action: the re-wrapped demo-staff.zod.ts TSDoc leaves "So" alone at the end of L20 before "every application used to carry"; reads fine, wraps oddly.
- Check-runs on the head (REST, read after they settled): every completed run is `success` or an opt-in/matrix `skipped`; none failed. All eight required contexts are `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI (skipped by its paths filter, as a spec-only diff is), Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI. `Lint · docs & code guards` (which carries `check:docs`, `check:doc-authoring`) and `Check Changeset` are `success`, which is the gate verdict on the regenerated mdx and the changeset's two declaration lines.
